newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Supply craft blasts off towards Mir space station.
newsitem.headline: Supply craft blasts off towards Mir space station.

text.p: A Russian Progress-35 cargo craft blasted off on Saturday with an emergency repair kit, oxygen reserves, food and water for the crippled Mir orbiting station.
Docking with Mir is expected on Monday.
Officials gathered in front of screens at mission control in Korolyov near Moscow applauded when Progress separated from the booster at an altitude of around 200 km (125 miles).

The craft is carrying 1.5 tonnes of supplies for the Mir space station, which carries a crew of two Russians and an American and lost up to half its electric power in a collision with an earlier unmanned supply craft on June 25.

"The crew is expecting special equipment from the Earth which will help them to make a visit to the damaged Spektr module," Viktor Blagov, deputy flight director, said on Friday, adding that parcels from the crew's families were also on board.
Shortly after Progress blasted off on Saturday, mission control made contact with Mir by radio. Crew commander Vasily Tsibliyev's first question was about the launch.
"It's O.K.," a mission control official told him.
